dedupe_keys.name: ghost and ephcc hardware in the loop models for testing microgrid controllers

description: GHOST (Grid Hardware Open Source Testbed) and the EPHCC repository provide real-time models and tools for testing commercial microgrid controllers in hardware-in-the-loop set-ups. The repository is maintained by the Electric Power HIL Controls Consortium with copyright held by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and the National Renewable Energy Laboratory registered GHOST in 2018 with Przemyslaw Koralewicz as developer after using it to procure a microgrid controller among competing vendors. Each controller was connected to an Opal-RT simulator running the same microgrid model with identical initial conditions and a 100-minute test sequence of disturbances in grid-connected and islanded modes, such as generator failures, storage trips, large load swings, high fault currents and loss of the swing bus. Recorded data are post-processed into performance scores for resilience, fuel use, grid interconnection, ancillary services and power quality. Tools include the Urban Banshee and a smaller remote microgrid model, test configuration and execution scripts, post-processing and an operator interface. Coverage is not tied to a place. The models are accessible on GitHub under the MIT licence at no cost. Caveats: Opal-RT hardware and Simulink are needed, the last commit was in 2018, and the README warns that models are at various stages of maturity. Simulation uses are benchmarking microgrid controllers against disturbances for resilience. Related records: data-certs-microgrid-test-bed gives field microgrid test data.
